classification.difficultyReason: Translate percentage changes through a cube-root model and its inverse cubic relationship.

content.prompt: Given that $p\propto\sqrt[3]{q}$, what is the effect on the following quantities? Give non-exact percentage changes to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Since $p=k\sqrt[3]{q}$, take the initial value $q=1$, so $p=k$.

After the increase, $q=1.2$:
$$\begin{align*}p_{\text{new}}&=k\sqrt[3]{1.2}\\p_{\text{new}}&\approx1.062658569k\end{align*}$$
The percentage increase is $(\sqrt[3]{1.2}-1)\times100\%\approx6.27\%$.

Since $p=k\sqrt[3]{q}$, take the initial value $q=1$, so $p=k$.

After the decrease, $q=0.95$:
$$\begin{align*}p_{\text{new}}&=k\sqrt[3]{0.95}\\p_{\text{new}}&\approx0.983047572k\end{align*}$$
The percentage decrease is $(1-\sqrt[3]{0.95})\times100\%\approx1.70\%$.

Rearrange the model:
$$\begin{align*}p^3&=k^3q\\q&=\frac{p^3}{k^3}\end{align*}$$
Take the initial value $p=1$, so $q=\frac{1}{k^3}$. After the increase, $p=1.1$:
$$\begin{align*}q_{\text{new}}&=\frac{1.1^3}{k^3}\\q_{\text{new}}&=\frac{1.331}{k^3}\end{align*}$$
Thus $q$ is $133.1\%$ of its initial value, an increase of $33.1\%$.

Take the initial value $p=1$, so $q=\frac{1}{k^3}$. After the decrease, $p=0.9$:
$$\begin{align*}q_{\text{new}}&=\frac{0.9^3}{k^3}\\q_{\text{new}}&=\frac{0.729}{k^3}\end{align*}$$
Thus $q$ is $72.9\%$ of its initial value, a decrease of $27.1\%$.
